originalTitle: British aid worker mistakenly identified as a survivor of Nepal-Tibet disaster
summary: More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000, including 36 British nationals, remain missing
content: A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight. Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges. After spending several days in a village near the Trishuli river in central Nepal, Chambers returned by helicopter to the capital, where he was greeted by police officers asking for his details. “I gave them my details, just abiding by the rules, and they obviously thought that I’d been rescued,” Chambers told the Press Association. Chambers appeared on a list of 119 names released by local authorities on Tuesday. An army spokesperson then told reporters at a press conference that a British national was among those rescued. “I was contacted by about 15 different journalists in the last few hours, just asking how I was and how I’m feeling after being rescued, and I had to say: ‘Well sorry, I haven’t been rescued,’” Chambers told PA. Those rescued included 118 Nepali nationals – 44 women and 74 men. Thirty-six British nationals are missing, the Foreign Office minister, Stewart Wood, told the House of Lords on Tuesday. The figure had previously been put at 33. Chambers was fined £49,000 after pleading guilty in June 2022 to breeding and selling dogs without a licence. The 45-year-old, who was the leader of a group of community independents on Gloucester city council until 2024, is due to face trial in November after denying he used homophobic slurs against a bar owner and former council worker. At least 1,050 people have been confirmed dead in Nepal since Wednesday’s flash floods, while Chinese state media said 66 people had been killed in Tibet. More than 4,000 people are still missing. Nepal’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region. This included 330 foreign nationals, the Nepalese tourist board said in an update on Tuesday. Preliminary analysis of satellite imagery suggests the collapse of a glacier high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the disaster. The collapse – so large it was initially recorded as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake – triggered a deadly torrent of water, mud and ice that tore along the Lhende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on Wednesday. Crews have faced dangerous and difficult conditions while searching unstable terrain and flood debris. Search efforts are now focused on attempts to reach about 600 workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at several hydropower stations in the region. “Massive work has been going on in the tunnel, all the tunnels,” the army spokesperson said on Tuesday. A rapid deployment rescue team from the UK arrived in Nepal on Saturday to provide support for Britons and their families as part of the government’s £5m commitment to support relief and recovery efforts. The Red Cross estimates that 93,000 people have been directly affected by the disaster.
chineseTitle: 英国救援人员被误认为尼泊尔西藏灾难幸存者
chineseSummary: 超过 1,000 人确认死亡，包括 36 名英国国民在内的 4,000 多人仍然失踪
chineseContent: 一名英国援助人员乘坐人道主义援助航班返回加德满都后，被尼泊尔当局误认为是获救的幸存者。 45 岁的前格洛斯特议员阿拉斯泰尔·钱伯斯 (Alastair Chambers) 表示，他上周飞往尼泊尔，向因桥梁倒塌而与外界隔绝的社区分发睡袋、食物和必需品。在尼泊尔中部特里苏利河附近的一个村庄待了几天后，钱伯斯乘坐直升机返回首都，在那里，警察迎接了他，询问他的详细信息。钱伯斯告诉记者协会：“我向他们提供了我的详细信息，只是遵守规则，他们显然认为我已经获救了。”钱伯斯出现在地方当局周二公布的 119 人名单上。军方发言人随后在新闻发布会上告诉记者，获救者中有一名英国国民。钱伯斯对 PA 表示：“在过去的几个小时里，大约 15 名不同的记者联系了我，只是询问我的情况以及获救后的感受如何，我不得不说：‘抱歉，我没有获救。’”获救者包括 118 名尼泊尔国民，其中 44 名女性和 74 名男性。英国外交部长斯图尔特·伍德 (Stewart Wood) 周二告诉上议院，有 36 名英国公民失踪。此前该数字为 33 只。钱伯斯在 2022 年 6 月承认无证饲养和销售狗的罪名后，被罚款 49,000 英镑。这名 45 岁的男子在 2024 年之前一直是格洛斯特市议会社区独立人士团体的领导人，他否认自己对酒吧老板和前议会工作人员使用仇视同性恋的诽谤性言论，将于 11 月接受审判。自周三山洪暴发以来，尼泊尔已确认至少有 1,050 人死亡，而中国官方媒体称，尼泊尔已造成 66 人死亡。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
